title: A map with gaps
hook: A blank part of a map can mean more than one thing.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: A toy map has animal sightings in surveyed places and no observations in an unsurveyed area. Does the blank area prove the animal is absent there?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: A toy map has animal sightings in surveyed places and no observations in an unsurveyed area. Does the blank area prove the animal is absent there?

claims.text: A toy map has animal sightings in surveyed places and no observations in an unsurveyed area. Does the blank area prove the animal is absent there? The first panel shows sightings in a surveyed area; the second marks a separate area that was not surveyed. A blank unsurveyed area does not establish absence. A targeted survey can reduce uncertainty, while imperfect detection still needs consideration.
claims.source: Stipulated illustrative scenario, not wildlife observations. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
No camera was placed in a forest patch and no sighting was recorded there. What can you conclude about absence? A lack of survey effort does not establish absence or presence.
